agreement.reading: The heat-wave ordering and the annual ordering are different questions and give different answers. A building that ranks far higher on the year has chronic facade load; one that ranks far higher on the wave has trapped air during an acute event. Where they agree the case is strong on both grounds.

reasons: Its facades accumulate 946 kelvin-hours above 35 °C over the year — modelled surface temperature, not air.
An average facade band takes 1,623 hours of direct sun a year and 524 kWh/m² of shortwave.
It peaks in July at 53 °C, and swings 27 K between summer and winter means.
It scores high on the heat wave and low on the year: its problem is acute, so relief measures matter more than fabric measures.
Winter facade mean is -1 °C, so any shading fitted for July also removes solar gain in January — the annual trade-off is real and is quantified in the what-if panel.
annual.basis: whole year, ERA5 bias-corrected anchor, analytic canyon shading — see heatcanyon/tiers.py

reasons: Measured: 4.4 h unbroken above 35 °C during the heat wave — no overnight recovery window.
Measured: 33 total hours above 35 °C across the seven-day event.
Modelled: 14 K spread between this building's hottest and coolest face — the exposure is one-sided and so is the remedy.
Modelled: pedestrian mean radiant temperature at the base peaks 31 K above air temperature (70 °C) — the sidewalk is far harsher than the air reading.
Modelled: WBGT 34.6 °C at the base exceeds the 32 °C threshold at which occupational guidance calls for work to stop.
People: 268 residential units — occupants are exposed overnight, not only during working hours.
People: built 1932; pre-war stock is unlikely to have central air conditioning or a performing envelope.

actions.title: High-albedo roof coating

actions.effect: Shaded MRT typically 15-25 K below sunlit MRT; air temperature 0.5-1.5 K

reasons: Its facades accumulate 1,870 kelvin-hours above 35 °C over the year — modelled surface temperature, not air.
An average facade band takes 1,845 hours of direct sun a year and 579 kWh/m² of shortwave.
It peaks in July at 55 °C, and swings 28 K between summer and winter means.
It scores high on the heat wave and low on the year: its problem is acute, so relief measures matter more than fabric measures.
Winter facade mean is -0 °C, so any shading fitted for July also removes solar gain in January — the annual trade-off is real and is quantified in the what-if panel.
annual.basis: whole year, ERA5 bias-corrected anchor, analytic canyon shading — see heatcanyon/tiers.py
